articles.title: PSG beat Man City 4-2 in Champions League thriller
articles.summary: PSG score three first-half goals, but an Erling Haaland brace nearly drags Manchester City back into the match.
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain further soured the mood at the Etihad Stadium as Manchester City’s first home game since the guilty verdict on widespread flouting of Premier League financial rules ended in a 4-2 Champions League defeat on Wednesday.

The European champions turned on the style to strike three times inside the opening 35 minutes through Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha.

But City stormed back in the second half as Erling Haaland scored twice on either side of Maghnes Akliouche’s strike, which briefly restored PSG’s three-goal cushion.

The 10-time English champions face swingeing sanctions unless they can successfully appeal last month’s ruling by an independent commission, which found the club guilty on more than 100 charges of financial impropriety.

City shrugged off the uncertainty over their future to win 3-0 at Liverpool on Sunday and remain top of the Premier League, but PSG showed why they are the favourites to win this competition for a third consecutive season.

Former City manager Pep Guardiola returned to the Etihad for the first time since his departure in May, sitting behind the club’s embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO, Ferran Soriano, in a show of solidarity.

City made passing reference to the guilty verdict with a lengthy pre-match video detailing the club’s historic moments of celebration both before and after an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008 that transformed their fortunes.

Behind one end, supporters unfurled a giant banner reading: “I’m City till I die.”

Yet the fighting talk in the stands didn’t match the on-field action as City were blown away by a scintillating first 45 minutes from the visitors.

Luis Enrique’s decision to leave Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the bench proved inspired, as it meant Doue started wide on the left.

Gianluigi Donnarumma had a point to prove after the Italian goalkeeper was let go by the PSG coach just months after helping deliver the club’s first Champions League title in 2025.

However, it turned out to be a night to forget for the giant Italian.

Donnarumma was caught out at his near post by Doue’s outside-the-box effort after a lightning counter-attack to open the scoring.

The move for the second goal two minutes later was even more impressive, as Doue and Dembele exchanged an elaborate one-two before the latter headed in at the far post.

Achraf Hakimi hit the post before Vitinha rattled in PSG’s third from the edge of the box.

Maresca responded with a triple substitution at half-time and managed to salvage some pride, even if the deficit proved too much to overturn.

Antoine Semenyo and Enzo Fernandez missed glaring chances to pull a goal back even before Haaland glanced home a header from Iliman Ndiaye’s cross.

Yet City were hit by a sucker punch when Donnarumma got a hand to Akliouche’s effort, but the ball looped high and spun back into the net.

Nuno Mendes made a brilliant clearance off his own line, and Haaland hit the bar before the Norwegian slotted home his second of the night.

Donnarumma saved a late Ferran Torres penalty, denying the French champions a fifth goal.

But in the battle between two state-backed projects that have reshaped European football, Qatar-owned PSG are the top dogs right now as City face a scandal that puts their trophy haul over the past 15 years in question.

articles.title: Lincoln 0-6 West Ham: Hammers net six against nine-man Imps
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln and West Ham at the Sincil Bank Stadium on Wednesday; Imps see two players sent off early before Hammers romp to victory.
articles.body:
The Imps had Tom Hamer sent off after just three minutes and Conor McGrandles followed him off the pitch 20 minutes later, with Konstantinos Mavropanos heading West Ham ahead on the stroke of half-time.

The second half was dominated by West Ham, with further goals coming from Edvin Austbo, Jarrod Bowen, Pablo and a Tomas Soucek brace, as the Imps manfully tried to keep the score down.

In their first league encounter for nearly 70 years, Lincoln made five changes from the 3-0 defeat to Sheffield United, with Hamer and Callum Elder making their first league starts for several weeks, while the West Ham side saw four new faces from their 1-1 draw with QPR.

Disaster struck for Lincoln with the game in its infancy, when the recalled Hamer - starting his first game since August 22 - was shown a straight red card by referee Andrew Kitchen after he lunged recklessly at Joel Veltman leaving the Hammers right-back in a heap on the floor.

City kept their composure in the face of adversity, though, more than matching their opponents as the half continued.

West Ham nearly took the lead in the 22nd minute when Bowen's corner was headed into the ground and wide by Mohamadou Kante.

City were then reduced to nine men a minute later when McGrandles shanked a pass back to keeper George Wickens from just inside his own half and as Bowen ran on to the wayward ball, the chasing Scot had no option but to grab a piece of the frontman's shirt and haul him to the ground 40 yards from goal, and being the last man, the inevitable red card was produced from Kitchen's top pocket.

City then had the next attack, with Ben House slicing a shot high and wide, with Mavropanos firing well over at the other end.

West Ham began to control proceedings and they struck just before the break, finally breaking City's brave resistance when Bowen's corner was headed in from close range by Mavropanos.

It took the Hammers just three minutes of the second half to double their lead when half-time substitute Austbo curled a powerful effort into the top corner from just inside the City box.

Bowen made it 3-0 a minute later, scuffing a left-footed shot that somehow trickled into the Imps net past an unsighted Wickens.

A Max Kilman volley flashed just wide for the visitors, before Pablo then made it 4-0 to West Ham, finishing off an Austbo pass.

Austbo brought another save out of Wickens and then sub Soucek added a fifth, lifting a shot over Wickens after 78 minutes.

Soucek made it six a minute from time, following up to slow home after Wickens had parried a Piroe shot.

"They are incredible fellas and top pros - they didn't let us down and they will learn from this as will we as a group and we'll move forward. These things happen.

"They were both red cards and two decisions the referee definitely got right. There were some I didn't particularly agree with in the first half, but the big decisions looked like they were correct.

"After three minutes I thought we responded pretty well with 10 men. I thought we had 20 minutes where we competed with West Ham.

"That's the overriding frustration of the evening where we didn't get a proper game. That 20 minutes makes me think we really could have troubled them. It was a tough night for everybody. We need to take a little bit of learning from it because we can do better, especially the goals, even with nine men.

"We have got to bounce back and pretty quickly as this was a pretty brutal experience against the best quality in the league."

West Ham head coach Nuno Espirito Santo:

"I credit Lincoln as even with one man down they were in the game and still creating a lot of problems for us. It became difficult to find the gaps.

"I think we made mistakes in terms of trying to rush things, trying shots from long range because you want to score so desperately.

"It changed after the second goal and we played much better, in terms of being patient, recycling of the ball and being clinical, which is what you want."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Man City 2-4 PSG: Erling Haaland scores twice but Enzo Maresca's side suffer first defeat of season in front of Pep Guardiola
articles.summary: Man City were beaten by PSG in first Champions League outing since Premier League handed down its guilty verdict; Pep Guardiola was in attendance alongside club's high-ranking executives; PSG scored three first-half goals to take control; Erling Haaland responded by scoring two
articles.body:
The reigning back-to-back European champions were keen to make their power felt early at the Etihad, in a game that made clear where the greater concentration of quality resides. Luis Enrique's side were breathtaking in the first half, a masterclass in effortless control with and without the ball.

Desire Doue scored from range. Ousmane Dembele rounded off a wonderful team move 99 seconds later. And Vitinha finished a brilliant first 45 minutes with a thumping finish from Warren Zaire-Emery's instinctive flick. "If you don't go toe-to-toe, you struggle," reflected Enzo Maresca.

A pair of Erling Haaland goals made the scoreline respectable after the interval, and City were good value for both breakthroughs, doing to PSG what had been done to them in the first period. They hit the woodwork a further two times in a half that became increasingly more frantic and transitional.

Despite wave after wave of attack and big chances missed, it was Gianluigi Donnarumma who failed to escape the glare of the spotlight, his poor handling gifting Maghnes Akliouche and the visitors a fourth. He atoned by denying Ferran Torres' woeful penalty attempt late on.

PSG's first-half blitz proved decisive and sobered the atmosphere around a fairly muted Etihad, but Maresca will take comfort from the way his side turned a would-be rout into a thrilling clash of titans.

PSG come out on top in battle of recent winners

As well as being two of the earliest clubs to fall foul of UEFA's financial rules back in 2014, Man City and PSG shared one other thing in common before combining to win three of the past four Champions League titles: They had won none of the previous 67.

Each lost their first Champions League final - PSG to Bayern in 2020 and City the following year to Chelsea. But with both clubs backed by free-spending owners from the Middle East, boasting some of the most talented squads in world football, that deficiency has since become a surplus.

With City now fighting against charges of financial rule-breaking on a domestic front, all of which the club deny, the decision was made for a show of unity on home turf. Guardiola was flanked by high-ranking executives in the terraces, including Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

They will have seen plenty they liked on the pitch, City's players appearing laser-focused on the job at hand despite the cloud of uncertainty that surrounds them. Ultimately, this is a defeat of fairly insignificant jeopardy where chances and goals made for a superb watch between two European contenders.

The world of football will continue to tune in to see how City handle whatever might come next. Whenever that might be.

Where do you start trying to make sense of that?

Pep Guardiola was back for a bonkers night, with his former side showing plenty of the strengths and weaknesses that displayed themselves in different ways during his tenure. The City fightback at least means his visit won't be characterised by a humbling defeat.

PSG were the better side overall and deserved the win, but on another night the scoreline could have been reversed, given the number of chances that went begging for the home side.

The City fans might not get to see their side in this competition next year, but as they made clear before kick-off, this is a fanbase that has stood by the club during dark times before, and is promising to do so again.

"It was a strange game. Two goals in two minutes created some problems for us. We were dead in the game, and then second half we created so many chances. Second half, we were good.

"We lost a bit of balance, distance between players, and we struggle first half. Second half we made changes and adjusted some things, then we were much better. These kind of teams, if you don't go toe-to-toe you struggle. We had to be more brave. Second half, we were.

"We are there, to be honest. My feeling is that we are close. It's already difficult against PSG, but then you concede two quick goals. We can learn from that and move on."

articles.title: Aston Villa 6-0 Fenerbahce: Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both score twice in big Champions League win
articles.summary: Match report as Aston Villa were big winners on the return of Champions League football to Villa Park; Fenerbahce were beaten 6-0 with Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley scoring two each for Unai Emery’s team as Johan Manzambi also scored in fine display
articles.body:
The impressive Johan Manzambi opened the scoring when his shot was deflected in off Fenerbahce captain Milan Skriniar to leave Ederson stranded and although Villa needed goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to save well from Vedat Muriqi it was all but over by the break.

Jackson's two first-half goals, both arrowed to Ederson's right, put Unai Emery's side three up by half-time. Fenerbahce's fans continued to chant away but there was no way back on what proved a comfortable night for Vila in front of the Prince of Wales.

The Turkish squad is packed with familiar names. Nathan Ake started, Romelu Lukaku came on, while Mason Greenwood's every touch was booed. But they had nobody with the exuberance of Manzambi or indeed the 18-year-old Ibrahim Mbaye out wide.

Manzambi won a penalty that Barkley tucked away expertly to make it four and another deflected shot brought the midfielder's second and his team's fifth. There was even time for Alysson to lay on the sixth for fellow substitute Tammy Abraham in the 90th minute.

It is two wins from two in the Champions League now, despite a less convincing start to the Premier League campaign for this new-look team. Villa's fans hoisted up a tifo declaring this the next chapter in their European story. It is good reading for them so far.

The decision to sell Ollie Watkins this summer would have left some Villa supporters concerned about how much the England forward would be missed this season but Jackson's start to life at Villa Park will have many feeling more encouraged.

The Senegal striker has scored in each of his last two Premier League appearances and now has three goals from two Champions League games too. The quality of his finishing has been a topic of debate throughout his career but he was utterly clinical in this game.

Jackson only turned 25 years old in June, whereas Watkins is 30. There are risks associated with Villa's rebuild but, with the new man having worked with Emery before at Villarreal, this is one buy that looks likely to work out well for the West Midlands side.

12 - GOAL! Manzambi's shot deflected in to put Villa ahead

17 - SAVE! Suzuki rushed out to save bravely from Muriqi

31 - GOAL! Jackson was put through by Kamara and scored

34 - CROSSBAR! Oguz Aydin rattled the crossbar from range

39 - GOAL! Jackson smashed in his second of the evening

68 - GOAL! Barkley converted a penalty won by Manzambi

72 - GOAL! Barkley's left-footed effort was deflected in

90 - GOAL! Alysson laid the sixth on a plate for Abraham

Aston Villa striker Nicolas Jackson speaking to TNT Sports:

"He [Johan Manzambi] is a top player. I'm very happy we're playing together. Hopefully we score many more goals together.

"He [Ibrahim Mbaye] is an amazing player. We're in the [Senegal] national team together so we have a good connection and we talk a lot. He's progressing so hopefully he'll get more time to play. He's very fast. It's good to have him."

On whether he wanted to take the penalty for a hat-trick chance: "Yeah, I wanted to take it, but there are rules. The most important thing is we win, but hopefully next time I'll get the hat-trick."

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking in the press conference:

"I am delighted for the first win at home. We needed it. In the first half, [even] winning 3-0 I was not so happy, like the last match. They didn't score but Zion played fantastic, they hit the crossbar, did not shoot well. But we wanted to control the match better.

"In the second half, we planned to correct it and I think we did it. After, we planned to stop them and we could score three more. They did not deserve 6-0 but for us it was very important how we achieved the first win at home."

Fenerbahce head coach Ismail Kartal speaking in the press conference:

"There is not much to say. The score is not earned, this is the top level of the Champions League and mistakes cost you a lot and that is what we experienced today.

"We could not have imagined a result like this. This is not acceptable. We apologise to all the supporters of the club. We have had our lesson tonight.

"We have an important league game in a few days. We should forget about tonight's game and concentrate on the next one."

Aston Villa have recorded their biggest ever win in major European competition, and their biggest victory under manager Unai Emery across all competitions.

Fenerbahce suffered their heaviest defeat in the Champions League on the night they played in the competition for the 42nd time.

Aston Villa have won 18 of their last 20 home games in major European competition, and are on the joint-longest active winning streak at home in such competitions (11 - level with Freiburg).

Aston Villa are one of two teams to score three first half goals in both of their opening two games of a Champions League campaign, alongside PSG also this season - the Villans are the second English team to do so in the European Cup, after Leeds United in 1969/70.

After scoring just once across their first four games this season, Aston Villa have since scored three or more goals in four of their six matches - no Premier League team has scored more times than the Villans since the start of the run.

articles.title: Real Madrid come from 3-1 down to beat Roma on Champions League travels
articles.summary: Real Madrid ease pressure on manager Jose Mourinho with a 4-3 win at his former club Roma in a Champions League classic.
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappe struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break.

Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

But Real scored three goals in the space of seven minutes late on, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espi, Endrick and ex-Roma defender Antonio Rudiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.

Mourinho was a popular figure, leading Roma to the UEFA Conference League title and an Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge.

The home crowd honoured the Portuguese with banners and chants in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years, and the hosts started strongly as Mario Hermoso forced Thibaut Courtois into a flying fingertip save.

Roma took a deserved lead when De Roon swept a shot past Courtois from 25 yards in the 20th minute, and almost doubled it when Malen’s powerful shot squirmed under Courtois before being plucked off the line.

However, one costly moment of switching off proved enough to send them back to square one within five minutes of the opener being scored.

Hermoso misjudged an interception to allow Mbappe a clear run at goal, and the French striker’s deflected shot flew into the roof of the net to level the scores with Real’s first meaningful chance of the game.

Mbappe marked his Champions League centurion status – he is the youngest player to reach the milestone, aged 27 – with his 72nd tournament goal, one that moved him into the all-time top five ahead of Real legend Raul Gonzalez.

The equaliser appeared to subdue Roma and steady Mourinho’s men, who twice threatened a second before the break as Marc Cucurella and Jude Bellingham came close.

But Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini insisted pre-match that Roma would not compromise on their full-throttle style regardless of opposition, and he was true to his word as they came out firing after the break.

Roma quickly retook the lead when half-time substitute Rodrigo Mora fed the ball to Malen, who finished brilliantly by taking the ball in his stride with his first touch and lifting it over Courtois with his second.

Things got even better for the Italians just six minutes later when Malen raced onto a through ball to power home his second, given following a VAR review after initially being flagged for offside.

Real looked for a response as Mbappe twice tested Pierluigi Gollini, before having his second goal of the night ruled out for offside.

But set-pieces proved to be the key to unlock the Roma defence, as Espi tucked home a close-range rebound from a header to pull one back before Endrick powered home a header from another corner just two minutes later.

The final blow was struck by Rudiger in the 90th minute, the defender getting in front of his marker to guide home a close-range finish and complete an extraordinary turnaround.

The result leaves Real Madrid with six points from their opening two league phase matches, while Roma are on one point.

Shakhtar Donetsk beat AEK Athens in London debut

Nomadic Ukrainian champions Shakhtar Donetsk celebrated moving into their new Champions League “home” at Stamford Bridge by storming back to beat AEK Athens 3-1.

Fans of the club turned up in the thousands to support the team, who emerged from the tunnel draped in blue-and-yellow national flags.

The Greek side took the lead in the 28th minute through Lovro Majer but Pedrinho levelled confidently from the penalty spot just six minutes later.

With about 10 minutes of normal time to go, Vinicius Tobias found the net from a tight angle and substitute Gleiker Mendoza made the game safe, smashing home after cutting in from the left.

The result leaves Shakhtar on four points after two games, following a draw against PSV Eindhoven in their opening match in the league phase of the Champions League.

Giant-killers Bodo sink Dortmund in Champions League

Fredrik Sjovold’s 52nd-minute strike secured a 1-0 victory for Bodo/Glimt over Borussia Dortmund, extending the Norwegian side’s remarkable home record against Europe’s elite.

Bodo were a cut above the 2024 Champions League runners-up and took the lead through Sjovold just after the break.

Dortmund improved in the final half hour but were unable to strike back, despite a late chance for Felix Nmecha.

Dortmund join Manchester City, Inter Milan and Sporting as recent big-name scalps on the artificial turf of Bodo’s Aspmyra stadium.

Aston Villa put six past Fenerbahce in record rout

Aston Villa recorded their biggest ever European victory as Nicolas Jackson inspired a 6-0 rout of Fenerbahce.

Unai Emery’s side won at Villa Park for the first time this season to maintain their 100 percent start in Europe’s elite club competition.

Swiss forward Johan Manzambi put Villa in front, and Jackson was on target twice before the interval.

Ross Barkley scored twice in the second half before Tammy Abraham’s late strike completed the rout.

articles.title: Mourinho: "Los madridistas no son estúpidos y yo voy a hablar para que se vea lo que pasa"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del entrenador del Real Madrid
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del entrenador del Real Madrid
articles.body: José Mourinho, entrenador del Real Madrid,acaba de pasar por la sala del prensa del estadio Olímpico para analizar lo vivido entre su equipo y la Roma. Mejores cuando peor van las cosas: "No estoy totalmente de acuerdo con Fede, ellos han planteado un partido diferente a todos los que han hecho hasta hoy, y de todos los que hemos analizado. Nos han atacado con tres jugadores por banda derecha, por ahí han ido los ajustes. Después encajamos un gol que no podemos hacer, no podemos hacer lo que hemos hecho en el centro del campo. Después es una rebeldía, entre comillas, es organizada, emocional. Sé perfectamente cómo juegan los equipos de Gasperini y nos ha sorprendido, pero en el fútbol no hay milagros, 90 minutos con esa intensidad no es posible". Lectura: "Vivimos dos partidos. En el primero, la Roma fue superior en todo; en los veinte minutos finales, era imposible parar al Madrid. El segundo gol que encajamos fue ridículo, impropio de este nivel. Cambiamos pensnando que ya daba igual encajar cuatro o cinco goles". Endrick: "Imposible que saga cedido. Sé la calidad que tiene". Más del partido: "Ha sido difícil, un rival que juega un deporte diferente al fútbol al que estamos acostumbrados, pero es muy difícil para ellos poder jugar con el ritmo y la intensidad y el hombre al hombre durante 90 minutos, ellos han merecido llegar con ventaja, aunque un par de goles que hemos encajado no me han gustado para nada, después hemos cambiado con coraje, de los jugadores. Un empate sería un punto positivo fuera ante un adversario importante y la victoria es importantísima para nosotros contra dos adversarios que son... no digo que los mejores porque queda el Arsenal, pero eran partidos muy complicados y nos metemos en una posición muy buena". Explicación: "La mala primera parte la culpa es mía. La buena segunda es de los jugadores". Más del partido: "En mi cabeza siempre quiero hacer el bien. Pienso en la meritocracia. El fútbol es un juego de 90 minutos, de mucha estrategia. Los rivales cuentan, y la Roma es muy fuerte. Un equipo terrible para jugar ante ellos. Sabía que la gasolina se les iba a acabar. Los cambios eran por eso. Nos han machacado en el primer tiempo. Nos han sorprendido con Sule. Muchos no contaban con Cucurella. Nos hemos reorganizado, pero nos comemos un gol que no se puede encajar". Vinícius: "¿Pensáis que es normal que un jugador de un equipo español sepa qué le cae de sanción? ¿No podía ser ahora, mañana? Nos metemos en un lío. En portugués se dice que hay gato escondido con la cola tapada. Ya no está escondido. Ya se hacen las cosas sin tapadera, sin vergüenza. ¿Quieres matar al jugador antes? Ya no es una pregunta. La primera pate es culpa mía. ¿Gesto en el cambio? Es normal. Lo que importa es que esba feliz poque hemos ganado. El jugador intenta bloquear sentimientos. Como me ha pasado a mí por jugara ante mi gente". Inflexión: "Si empezamos como acabamos, nos meten cinco. Hay momentos y momentos. Tenía cambios para hacer. Se iban a cansar, iban a llegar las tarjetas". El gato y la Federación: "Pido respeto. No me parece inocente tener que jugar en Atenas y luego un partido tan duro como el del Valencia el sábado. No me como las explicaciones de la televisión. No es una decisión inocente. Los madridistas no son estúpidos y yo voy a hablar para que se vean las cosas. No merece más comentario lo de Vinicius". Remontada: "Es distinta la Liga que la Champions. Seis puntos ante equipos muy duros: Inter y Roma. Con seis puntos estamos bien situados. El año pasado tenía cero con el Benfica". Espí: "Está creciendo, me gusta mucho. Pero si la pregunta es si voy a sentar a Mbappé, la respuesta es no".

articles.title: FIFA Reportedly to Make Rule Change After USMNT's Folarin Balogun World Cup Red Card Controversy
articles.summary: FIFA is reportedly set to abolish the rule that currently allows for red-card suspensions to be delayed and served in the future after this summer's World Cup controversy involving USMNT striker Folarin Balogun.
articles.body:
FIFA is reportedly set to abolish the rule that currently allows for red-card suspensions to be delayed and served in the future after this summer's World Cup controversy involving USMNT striker Folarin Balogun.

According to ESPN , one of the top items on the upcoming FIFA council's meeting "is a motion to amend FIFA rules to prohibit the suspensions of automatic one-match bans in the future. The decision by FIFA's disciplinary committee to suspend the ban imposed on Balogun sparked outcry that it amounted to political interference, after U.S. President Donald Trump admitted he had personally asked [FIFA president Gianni Infantino] to review the ban. FIFA members have criticized Infantino for his ties to Trump and potential conflicts of interest."

Infantino is already facing extensive pressure to resign from UEFA, AFC and CONCACAF following his failed attempt to kickstart the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, a scheme that sought to sell stakes in the World Cup and other events to private investors.

But his handling of the Balogun situation was nearly as controversial. Per ESPN, "Football Association chair and FIFA vice president Debbie Hewitt... wrote to Infantino last month calling for the release of documents related to the Balogun case."

The FIFA president has maintained that he wasn't a part of the decision and that it was handled by the disciplinary committee.

Balogun, 25, was given a controversial red card during a Round of 32 win over Bosnia & Herzegovina. Generally, a straight red results in a one-match ban for the following contest, but FIFA invoked a rule allowing the punishment to be pushed out further into the future, causing an enormous controversy in the process.

He then started the team's 4-1 loss against Belgium in the Round of 16 and said the situation—and widespread furor that accompanied it—negatively impacted the USMNT.

"I could almost see within my teammates a bit of nerves because it was something that's so unique," could," he told CBS Mornings in July. "But the closer we got to the game, I tried to just focus as best as I could."

"When something is not intentional... it should never be a red card," he added. "So it was just an unfortunate situation and I think, you know, it put a lot more pressure on us than we needed."

articles.title: Lisandro Martínez entona el 'mea culpa': "Hablé desde la frustración"
articles.standfirst: El central argentino publicó un comunicado a raíz de sus palabras después de la derrota contra el Atlético de Madrid
articles.summary: El central argentino publicó un comunicado a raíz de sus palabras después de la derrota contra el Atlético de Madrid
articles.body: La derrota contra el Atlético de Madrid cayó como una 'bomba' en el banquillo de un Manchester United que ha arrancado la temporada lejos del nivel esperado. Lisandro Martínez implosionó en zona mixta y disparó directamente contra la cúpula directiva. Horas después, ha entonado el 'mea culpa'. "Tras todo lo que se ha dicho sobre mis comentarios de ayer, quiero compartir algunos pensamientos sobre lo que dije y cómo me siento. Después del partido, hablé desde el enojo y la frustración por no haber conseguido el resultado que todos queríamos", explicó el defensor argentino. "Quienes me conocen saben cómo vivo el fútbol: con pasión, compromiso y un enorme deseo de ganar. Y cuando las cosas no salen como queremos, duele, especialmente cuando se representa a un club con la historia y la estatura del Manchester United". "Mis palabras reflejan cómo me siento y cuánto quiero ver a este club compitiendo por los mayores honores. Esos altos estándares son parte de cómo veo el fútbol y la responsabilidad que conlleva llevar esta camiseta". Una vez más, eso sí, recalcó cuáles son los estándares del club. "Cuando hablo de querer más, me refiero a la ambición que todos debemos tener como parte de este club. Seguir creciendo, hacernos más fuertes y tener todo lo necesario para competir al más alto nivel. Estos son estándares a los que todos debemos aspirar, empezando por mí". En cualquier caso, también hizo autocrítica. "Sé que, ante todo, somos nosotros, los jugadores, quienes tenemos que rendir, y me pongo a la cabeza de esa responsabilidad. Necesitamos exigimos aún más a nosotros mismos y trabajar juntos para llevar al Manchester United de vuelta a la cima". "Creo en mis compañeros de equipo, en nuestro entrenador y en todos los que trabajan para ayudar a este club a avanzar. Estoy convencido de que el camino a seguir es seguir trabajando juntos, con ambición y compromiso. Mi objetivo ha sido el mismo desde el primer día: ganar, competir al más alto nivel y darlo todo por este escudo", finalizó.

articles.title: "Es importante ganar, pero también lo es cómo se gana"
articles.standfirst: Pellegrini, encantado con el seis de seis puntos en Champions
articles.summary: Pellegrini, encantado con el seis de seis puntos en Champions
articles.body: El técnico del Betos, Manuel Pellegrini, se mostró radiante al terminar el partido tras la victoria: "Para mí es muy importante ganar, lo más importante, pero también la forma ganar porque las hay distintas. Por fortuna tenemos las ideas claras y salimos desde el primer minuto a jugar así". "El ambiente ha sido tremendo, para un equipo con apenas dos Champions en 120 años y que llevaba casi un cuarto de siglo esperando, casi una generación, y me alegra porque damos una alegría la gente. Seis puntos, cerca del objetivo que es pasar de ronda, pero hasta que la matemática no lo diga..." afirmó. Pellegrini agradeció al compromiso del equipo ante un rival tan físico como el Oporto: "Lo hablamos antes del partido, que era importante la recuperación en la salida, que la suelen hacer por el centro pero la intensidad de tremenda y también la pudimos mantener en la segunda parte porque los que entraron lo hicieron comprometidos y pudimos mantenerlo. Los tres puntos me dejan muy contento pero el rendimiento del equipo también". Pellegrini cree que la victoria es merecida: "Ha sido una noche muy importante, fundamental conseguir estos puntos. En la primera parte fuimos muy superiores y el 0-0 no reflejaba la verdad de lo ocurrido y en la segunda tuvimos el 2-0 con el poste de Antony y ellos en dos ocasiones puntuales le dieron la vuelta, además es un equipo grande, de Champions, acostumbrado a estos partidos, pero mantuvimos la calma y pudimos remontar el marcador".

articles.title: Antony: "Estamos construyendo ese espíritu de ganar"
articles.standfirst: Feliz por el pleno de triunfos de su equipo en la Liga de Campeones
articles.summary: Feliz por el pleno de triunfos de su equipo en la Liga de Campeones
articles.body: El extremo brasileño del Betis Antony dos Santos se mostró muy feliz por el pleno de triunfos de su equipo en la Liga de Campeones de fútbol, tras vencer por 3-2 al Oporto en la segunda jornada, y destacó que están "construyendo ese espíritu de ganar" y que esta nueva victoria redobla su "confianza". "Cuando salimos al campo, me emocioné por la afición y por todo, después de veintiún años sin jugar 'Champions' en nuestra casa. Esto es muy importante para todos. Ha sido una noche muy dura, pero conseguimos la victoria", afirmó en declaraciones a Movistar+ el atacante de Osasco (estado de Sao Paulo). Antony subrayó la relevancia del nuevo triunfo logrado por el Betis y la buena imagen dada por su equipo. "Lo más importante es que peleamos hasta el final, estamos construyendo ese espíritu de ganar y tener esta secuencia de victorias nos da más confianza para seguir adelante", recalcó. El internacional brasileño incidió en esa idea, manifestó que en el Betis están "creando un plantel muy fuerte, y ahí está esta secuencia de buenos de resultados", y añadió que aunque "queda mucho por delante, es muy importante para ganar confianza, sobre todo ganando en casa". "Tengo mucho orgullo por todo el equipo. Estamos creando ese espíritu, que es lo importante, para seguir adelante", concluyó.

articles.title: Farioli: "Hemos hecho muchas cosas bien para lograr más"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Oporto lamentó la derrota por 3-2
articles.summary: El entrenador del Oporto lamentó la derrota por 3-2
articles.body: El entrenador del Oporto, el italiano Francesco Farioli, lamentó la derrota por 3-2 en el campo del Betis en la segunda jornada de la fase liga de la Liga de Campeones, en la que aún no han puntuado, y consideró que en Sevilla su equipo hizo "muchas cosas bien para lograr más, pero la 'Champions' exige dar más". "Les he dicho a mis jugadores en el vestuario que estos dos partidos de 'Champions' -tras el 0-2 ante el Manchester City y el 3-2 contra el Betis- estaban abiertos para haber tenido la oportunidad de sacar un resultado positivo, pero también es verdad que nos hemos enfrentado a dos rivales en sus mejores momentos y este tipo de cosas pueden afectar", indicó en rueda de prensa. El técnico del Oporto admitió que no les "gusta perder dos partidos", pero sostuvo que "hay que ponerlo todo en su contexto" y también valoró el potencial ofensivo del Betis, pues "esta noche cada vez que el balón llegaba a sus delanteros generaban una oportunidad de gol o de disparo", por lo que su equipo tiene que "hacerlo mejor". En cualquier caso, afirmó que "en la actitud de defender" no ve "cosas distintas" y son "un equipo haciendo todo lo posible para recuperar y proteger la portería", y cree que volverán "pronto" a su "mejor nivel", además de defender a Francisco Moura, que cometió el penalti que originó el 3-2, y no quiso personalizar posibles errores en ningún jugador. Farioli lamentó esta nueva derrota en la máxima competición europea en "un partido difícil de controlar desde el banquillo" y consideró que la clave de la derrota de su equipo fue "la precipitación en el último pase". Argumentó que "con el balón, en los primeros 70 metros", su equipo "estuvo bien, haciéndolo llegar a (Alan) Varela para crear ocasiones", pero la falta de acierto en el último tercio de campo propició un "resultado decepcionante" en un "partido loco" y en el que esgrimió que el Oporto pudo "haber marcado dos o tres goles más". El técnico toscano recordó que, después del 1-2 del español Samu Aghehowa, el Oporto gozó de "dos o tres ocasiones para sentenciar el encuentro, situaciones muy favorables para marcar", pero sus hombres no supieron "controlar el partido en este tipo de ambiente, sobre todo para un equipo" como el suyo, "que siempre quiere más". También destacó "el nivel individual de los jugadores" del Betis, "que pueden generar oportunidades casi en solitario", además de tener "buenos extremos para abrir el campo", y agregó que esta "segunda derrota" les deja "una energía negativa" porque piensa que habrían "merecido algo más", por lo que incidió en que hay "aspectos que mejorar".

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez says his outburst came out of 'anger and frustration'
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez says he "spoke out of anger and frustration" when launching a scathing attack on the club's hierarchy.
articles.body:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez says he "spoke out of anger and frustration" when launching a scathing attack on the club's hierarchy.

The Argentina international criticised United for not strengthening the squad in the summer following qualification for the Champions League in comments made after the 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League group phase on Tuesday.

Martinez said he expected more investment in the United squad and "more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]".

However, while he stopped short of an apology, he said he has "belief in my team-mates, our manager [Michael Carrick] and everyone working to help this club move forward".

"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted," he wrote in a social media post.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United .

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours.

"Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club.

"To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level.

"These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me."

Man Utd defender Martinez issues scathing attack on board

Wilcox the target again in another damaging Man Utd fallout

Manchester United have not won in five games since beating Sabah in the Champions League on 10 September.

They have won just two of their nine games this season and are 13th in the Premier League with six points from as many games.

Martinez's contract expires at the end of the season and United have the option to extend it by another year.

He added: "I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility.

"We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

"I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward.

"I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.

"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."

Manchester United 's next game will be at Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday, 18 October.

articles.standfirst: La Real se mide hoy a un conjunto belga que no ha caído aún de local en 2026 y al que debe derrotar si quiere seguir aspirando al top 8 de esta Europa League
articles.summary: La Real se mide hoy a un conjunto belga que no ha caído aún de local en 2026 y al que debe derrotar si quiere seguir aspirando al top 8 de esta Europa League
articles.body: La Real Sociedad tratará de poner hoy fin a la gran racha de 13 partidos sin perder como local del Union Saint-Gilloise, todos los que ha disputado este 2026 y el último del pasado año, y traerse de Bélgica a San Sebastián una victoria que le permita recuperar los puntos, sobre todo, y el optimismo perdidos para esta Europa League tras el 1-2 frente al Bournemouth en Anoeta, en la jornada inaugural. El sueño en esta competición sigue siendo llegar muy lejos. La Real llega a esta cita en un gran momento, como hemos destacado estos días previos en MARCA, ya que ha vuelto a ser sexta en la clasificación de LaLiga 29 meses después, gracias a los 13 puntos sumados de los últimos 18, el tercer equipo que más, y lo ha hecho con hasta 10 goleadores diferentes. Y es que Matarazzo ha conseguido que su equipo saque adelante sus partidos sin depender tanto como antes de las dianas de Mikel Oyarzabal y Take Kubo, aún inéditos este curso, u Orri Óskarsson, el otro gran realizador de la pasada campaña. Los tres, por cierto, apuntan a volver hoy al equipo titular, después de no jugar el primero más que 40 minutos ante el Dépor, una cita en la que el segundo no saltó al césped y que el tercero se perdió por estar sancionado. Serán algunos de los futbolistas con los que el técnico de Nueva Jersey tiene pinta que va a refrescar su once inicial. Marrero en la portería, Fort y Zubeldia en la defensa, Gorrotxategi y Turrientes en el centro del campo y Kubo en el ataque pueden ser otras de las caras nuevas. Sería una sorpresa que muchos de estos hombres no tuvieran hoy la oportunidad de demostrar que pueden seguir siendo considerados como titulares, pese a que últimamente les esté tocando ser más suplentes. La idea de la Real será ser el primer equipo en vencer a domicilio a su rival de esta tarde en este 2026, después de que 13 no lo hayan podido hacer, entre ellos el Atalanta y el Bodo Glimt en la Champions, y el Anderlecht, el Brujas o el Genk, en el campeonato belga, en el que aún no ha caído en este curso. Por si fuera poco, el Union Saint-Gilloise se estrenó en esta fase Liga de la Europa League con un contundente 0-3 en la visita a un viejo conocido de la Real, el Viktoria Plzen, por lo que superarle sería privar que uno de los líderes hiciera pleno y empezar a situarse en la parte media de la clasificación, sin perder de vista los ocho primeros puestos que llevan directamente a los octavos. La Real estará arropado por unos 550 seguidores, a los que el club txuriurdin ha enviado sus localidades a través del correo electrónico. El de encuentro de todos ellos será Oude Markt, una plaza situada en el centro de la ciudad, con varios bares y restaurantes. Las 14.00 horas es a la que se pide a la afición realista que haga acto de presencia, para ir desde ese lugar al campo, un recorrido de sólo 15 minutos, recordando la prohibición de consumir bebidas alcohólicas en la calle. La grada destinada a la afición visitante se encuentra ubicada en la puerta ‘Away Entrance – Tervuursevest’ y el deseo es abandonarla unas horas más tarde tras disfrutar de un triunfo.

articles.summary: Zaid, Mangala, Enes Ünal y Azón son bajas ante un cuadro rumano que llega lanzado
articles.body: Vuelve el Eurogeta seis años después y lo hace con el mismo sello, el de su entrenador Bordalás, pero con distintas sensaciones. Aquel equipo que jugó los octavos de final de la Europa League ante el Inter venía de tocar la cima tras aquella eliminatoria para la historia ante el Ajax que solo el covid impidió comprobar dónde estaba su límite. Hoy, los azulones han perdido talento, pero Europa es el lugar perfecto para recuperar la identidad tras las malas sensaciones que su entrenador señaló en el Camp Nou. Por tanto, Craiova es una prueba para un equipo que llega con dudas. No hay que olvidar que enfrente está el vigente campeón rumano, que viene de ganar sus cinco últimos partidos oficiales y cuyos datos goleadores asustan: 25 tantos en 11 jornadas de Liga. El Universitatea contará con un estadio Ion Oblemenco lleno que intentará llevar en volandas a los suyos para comenzar bien el camino europeo y colarse al menos en el top 24 de la Conference. Bordalás no tiene muchas opciones para hacer rotaciones, ya que cuenta con cuatro bajas de teóricos titulares y no puede contar con el reciente fichaje, Dani Carvajal, que no está inscrito y que no podría estrenarse en Europa hasta el hipotético caso de superar la fase liga y jugar eliminatorias, que será cuando se abra el proceso de inscripción de nuevos futbolistas. Arriba es donde más ausencias tiene Bordalás, ya que a la sabida de Enes Ünal se unió Iván Azón, por lo que puede ser el momento del estreno de Borja Mayoral como titular después de un inicio de temporada en el que el parleño no ha contado con la confianza del entrenador. El Getafe no estará solo en el estadio Ion Oblemenco, ya que más de 300 aficionados azulones estarán presentes en las gradas, invitados por el club presidido por Ángel Torres. El fútbol español estará muy pendiente de lo que haga un Getafe cuyos puntos son fundamentales si España quiere tener un quinto equipo para la próxima Liga de Campeones. El Rayo hizo mucho el año pasado y ahora le toca al Getafe seguir su estela en una Conference en la que parte como favorito para colarse en el top 24, pese a las dificultades de una corta plantilla y una exigencia máxima con rivales de más enjundia que nunca.

articles.title: SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey Talks CFP Expansion, Says Decision Will Come 'Sooner Rather Than Later'
articles.summary: SEC commissioner Greg Sankey revealed that a decision regarding the potential expansion of the College Football Playoff is on the horizon.
articles.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey revealed that a decision regarding the potential expansion of the College Football Playoff is on the horizon.

"We'll make some final decisions — probably sooner rather than later — is my expectation," Sankey said Wednesday, per Scott Dochterman of The Athletic.

Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger previously reported that the SEC initially opposed the Big Ten's proposal to expand the CFP from 12 to 24 teams, but the SEC has become open to the updated format.

"Attitudes change over time and perspectives change, and so we'll see where that leads us from a final decision standpoint," Sankey said, per Dochterman. "I think in general, we have achieved some of the progress we've expected on scheduling commitments. We'll see if we can finalize those across the nation."

The ACC and Big 12 have expressed support for a 24-team playoff, while the expansion decision will ultimately be made by the SEC and Big Ten.

"More access is good for this conference," Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark told Dochterman. "If we had the 24-team format last year, we would have gotten five schools in, and that would be great for this conference. Not good, but great."

If the 24-team format is adopted, Power 4 conference championship games would be eliminated in order to schedule the additional playoff contests. All of the Power 4 conference championship games have a media value of at least $200 million, according to ESPN's Heather Dinich .

Sankey acknowledged that there are still hurdles to clear in CFP discussions on Wednesday.

"We've worked through and continue to consider and work through those issues," Sankey said, per Dochterman. "I think there's an openness to Playoff expansion on our part."

The deadline for a possible change to the CFP format is Dec. 1, although officials can agree to an extension.

articles.title: Manchester City 2-4 PSG: Pep Guardiola returns but European champions humble City
articles.summary: On their return to Etihad Stadium Manchester City put on a show of defiance - even in the face of a PSG masterclass, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Manchester City returned to the welcoming surroundings of home for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations awash with defiance and presenting an 'us against the world' united front.

Pep Guardiola was back at the place he decorated with success for a decade in a public show of support to embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano, the Catalan a low-key presence clad in a flat cap sitting a row behind the pair.

If his appearance was relatively under the radar, the fact that he chose a game certain to attract a global audience to make his return was heavy with significance.

Guardiola is ignoring the outside noise to back his former bosses to clear their name on appeal after the guilty verdict passed down by an independent commission.

The stand bearing his name was emblazoned with a 'CTID' - City 'Til I Die - mosaic, while the build-up to kick-off saw a display of fireworks and pyrotechnics worthy of several rock concerts.

The strategy to show an unabashed City ready to face down any enemy was going well, until the game kicked off and Champions League holders Paris St-Germain produced a ruthless first-half reality check cloaked within the brutal beauty of their football.

With City providing a dramatic backdrop off the pitch, the game more than matched the setting. A second-half revival ensured embarrassment was avoided - and instead gave us a classic.

Man City suffer as PSG masterclass sets up Champions League win

How much did Man City's rule breaking cost your team?

City's first step back into the limelight on the hostile territory of Anfield on Sunday ended with a 3-0 win at Liverpool and wild celebrations.

Here, with Guardiola watching on from the directors' box with an agonised expression mirroring that of successor Enzo Maresca in his technical area, City ran headlong into a whirlwind of magnificent football from Luis Enrique's PSG, the half-time scoreline of 3-0 actually doing them a kindness.

To City's great credit, and also Maresca's after he made three half-time changes, they responded superbly after the break, creating a host of chances before eventually losing 4-2.

It did not retrieve what was lost in the first half, but it did at least allow City's fans to ramp up a frenzied atmosphere and give their team a rousing send-off at the final whistle.

In these surroundings, there was no question of any backlash against City's Abu Dhabi-based owners, despite the fact they were found guilty of such serious financial charges to leave the club in crisis and attracting pariah status.

The damage was done in PSG's staggering opening 45 minutes, with Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha the scorers as City were ripped apart.

A game that began in a wall of sound, with Guardiola's name resounding around the stadium at kick-off, was reduced to stunned silence in the first 15 minutes.

City, so composed and ordered amid the toxicity of Anfield on Sunday, were shell-shocked on home territory as even born streetfighters such as Enzo Fernandez were reduced to chasing shadows.

The players who rose in the face of the storm raging around Manchester City at Liverpool suddenly looked like they were carrying the weight of the world on their shoulders, which made their outstanding display after the break even more praiseworthy.

Guardiola looked just as engaged as when he was manager

Erling Haaland gave City hope, which looked to be snuffed out when goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who had a very poor night against his former club, saved from Maghnes Akliouche, only to see the ball drop behind him into the net.

Guardiola sometimes looked just as engaged as he did when he prowled the touchline here at Etihad Stadium, collecting the trophies now being called into question.

When Josko Gvardiol had a header cleared off the line Guardiola clutched his face in anguish. When Haaland scored a goal that threatened to offer City an unlikely lifeline, he remained seated but pumped his fists into the air.

If the Catalan was a neutral observer, he would have relished a game of glorious chaos, the first half embellished by PSG before City mounted superb momentum after the break.

As a lover of pure football with the emphasis placed firmly on attack, he may have enjoyed it anyway. The post-match discussion with Maresca would certainly have had a busy agenda.

Maresca felt he saw enough to give City hope should they meet PSG again later in the Champions League, despite the manner in which they were dismantled in the first half.

"I really like playing against PSG because they are brave," said Maresca. "We know the way they want to press. They go man-to-man and they are very dynamic on the ball. They are the best team in Europe. They play fantastic football.

"But I think we are there. The reason why we struggled was because we conceded two early goals so quickly. When you are on the pitch you might think this is difficult, but in the second half we created enough to maybe deserve something.

"We feel sorry for the first half but I think we're quite happy now."

Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha, watching for Match of the Day, described it as "great entertainment", but "not a normal game of football".

"I don't feel like both teams were going at it at the same time," he said. "In the first half, PSG were excellent and City looked really off the pace. As a consequence they were heavily punished and the game basically left them.

"But then in the second half they have made some changes, they have rallied, knowing they are playing in front of their own crowd and their performance had to be better. So, it was more aggressive and more on the front foot, and that's why we saw those crazy scenes where it was shot after shot by City.

"If these two teams had played this game in matchweek six or seven, it would not have looked like this. There would have been more defensive solidity from both sides and they would probably have approached the game in a different manner.

"But at this stage, as we have kind of seen with some of the other games tonight, it is just goals, goals and more goals."

Either way, the superb Enrique remains the scourge of the Premier League, adding another win against City to a Champions League victims list that includes Liverpool , Aston Villa , Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal , in a semi-final then last season's final.

Enrique is currently master of all he surveys in Europe as leader of this wonderful PSG team.

For Maresca and City, it is back to domestic business at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday – and all the uncertainty that brings with the Premier League in a state of limbo as they await sanctions and the result of their appeal.

articles.title: Defiance or denial? Inside Manchester City’s bubble, decked with inflatable bananas
articles.summary: Stepping inside the plush halls of Manchester City’s Etihad Stadium before Wednesday’s Champions League match against Paris Saint-Germain felt a bit like walking into an alternative universe.
articles.body: Stepping inside the plush halls of Manchester City’s Etihad Stadium before Wednesday’s Champions League match against Paris Saint-Germain felt a bit like walking into an alternative universe. Despite all the criticism that has pummeled the club since it was found guilty of over 100 charges relating to financial breaches, you could be fooled into thinking nothing was wrong. In recent weeks, the Premier League side has been called a cheater and a liar by many. Those who love the club could only watch as its past successes were belittled and its fans became the butt of jokes – or, as one supporter told me, shouted at in a grocery store for wearing the club colors. But despite the torrent of abuse from all angles, City has pleaded its innocence, appealing the guilty verdict and promising its players, staff and fans that it’s entirely innocent – arguing it’s merely the victim of a witch hunt. That message has landed well internally, at least publicly. Manager Enzo Maresca has brushed aside a barrage of tricky questions about the topic with a smile, while players, both past and present, have toed the line. The fans are certainly playing their part as well. In a storm that had nothing to do with them, many have bought into the pantomime of it all, relishing their role as the arch villains of English soccer. It’s not as though fans were crying in the stands worrying about what the sanctions could entail – be that transfer bans, points deductions or even relegation from the Premier League entirely. Instead, the concourses on Wednesday were full of groups of supporters manifesting ways in which the appeal would be successful. Optimism, blind or otherwise, was the name of the game. To sell that dream further, the stadium was treated to a light show before kickoff, accompanied by a montage which showed past occasions when City had overcome the odds. It was another thinly veiled message to tell supporters not to worry. And, despite the heavy 4-2 loss against PSG, there were no signs of anyone breaking rank. Finding hope in bananas Unlike at Liverpool last weekend, when the team was booed from pillar to post, the Etihad’s four walls felt like an oasis on Wednesday. If you didn’t know the context or hadn’t been following the news of the possible sanctions hovering over City’s head, you’d think this was a club totally in tune with one another. Fully dosed up on an ‘us against them’ mentality, the togetherness between the players, manager and the fans is almost enviable. And in the face of such adversity, the fanbase has opted for a measure of gallows humor – symbolized by hundreds of inflatable yellow bananas that punctuated the capacity crowd that was treated to an enthralling match against PSG. Even when City fell behind, the bananas were waving enthusiastically wherever you looked. Such an oddity does have meaning, though. The inflatables are a throwback to the 1980s when Manchester City was relegated to the second tier of English soccer. In an attempt to lighten the mood around the club at the time, fans nicknamed their then journeyman striker Imre Varadi as ‘Imre Banana’ and have been bringing their inflatables ever since. Those bananas are now working harder than ever in the current circumstances. UAE vs Qatar There was something perfect about City’s opponent in what was the first home match since all this news broke. Just as City has been backed by the United Arab Emirates since its takeover in 2008, PSG is backed by Qatar. In 2014, both teams were charged with breaking “Financial Fair Play” rules by UEFA – the governing body that runs the Champions League. After a years-long process, though, both PSG and Manchester City escaped relatively lightly and City seemingly found a friend in the Parisians this time around. PSG manager Luis Enrique told reporters before the match that he’d hoped City would escape serious sanctions from the Premier League, a rare voice of support in a pretty deriding domestic crowd. The PSG faithful, however, were less kind – jeering the City players as they came out for the warm-up and seemingly reveling in their host’s disappointment in the defeat. In truth, a night that started with so much gusto fell a bit flat from City’s perspective. Even the presence of former manager Pep Guardiola in the stands couldn’t turn the team’s fortunes around. After leaving this summer following ten incredible, trophy-laden seasons in charge, Guardiola was welcomed back at the Etihad as Manchester City continues to keep up appearances. The Spaniard has been a strong voice for unity since the verdict, calling on everyone associated with the club to stick together and trust the ownership. His face appearing on the big screen was naturally greeted by cheers of adoration from the stands and would normally have been a pure reason to smile. But as with everything about City at the moment, the context spoke so much louder. It’s not normal for a legendary manager to return so quickly to a club he just left. This felt like another ploy from City to yet again prove that nothing is wrong, and everything will be totally okay. What the future holds But step outside of the Etihad Stadium and the harsh reality quickly dawns. Supporters don’t seem keen to talk to the media about the charges, even less so the guilty verdict, and almost all parrot the same response: ‘Wait for the appeal.’ But blaming others and kicking the problem down the road won’t, and never will, make the problem go away. And while the Champions League might eventually prove a tonic during a tough season, the club will be reminded of its very real danger every time it plays a Premier League match. It’s in those moments, when facing clubs directly impacted by the saga, that City will face its toughest tests of the season. And with the appeal process still months from completion, the farcicality of this whole episode will rear its head time and time again – no matter how many inflatable bananas the fans manage to blow up and how much the club stresses that everything is definitely still okay.

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise
articles.summary: Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy after their Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox
articles.body:
Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.

He said: "Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel.

"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.

"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett :

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Sky Sports News has also been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

United's bosses have yet to decide whether to discipline Martinez for his comments, when he said: "I expect more from our technical director [meaning director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Sky Sports News has been told there is anger and bemusement at what Martinez said, both in the United boardroom and in the changing room, with at least one other player challenging him over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

The implication that Martinez doesn't think his team-mates are good enough to compete has not gone down well with other players.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Martinez remains a key part of Michael Carrick's squad and United's bosses know they have to handle this situation carefully.
